description: The plot titled “Hidden State Mean” illustrates how the absolute mean of hidden states varies across network layers for three conditions (before gate, after gate, and a baseline). The x-axis is labeled “Layer,” uses a linear scale, and spans approximately layers 0 to 23 with tick labels shown at 0, 5, 10, 15, and 20. The y-axis is labeled “Abs Mean,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from about 0 up to roughly 4.5 with major ticks at integer values (0, 1, 2, 3, 4). A blue dashed line (legend: “hidden state mean before gate, avg 0.71”) starts near 0.0 at layer 0, rises to around 0.25 by about layer 2, stays around ~0.2–0.4 through the mid layers, then increases more noticeably after about layer 18 (around ~0.5–0.9), jumps to roughly ~2.6 around layer 21, and ends near ~4.4 at the final layer. An orange dotted line (legend: “hidden state mean after gate, avg 0.05”) stays close to zero across all layers, beginning near ~0.0 and gradually increasing to around ~0.1 by the last layers. A green solid line (legend: “hidden state mean of baseline, avg 0.04”) also remains near zero, starting near ~0.0 and slowly rising across layers to approximately ~0.1–0.12 at the end.
